Conjecture Some functional of the Wedderburn-weighted Hoefsmit character data at q_0 carries nuclear shell structure. The Wedderburn-weighted nuclear character signal \delta^2\Phi(Z), computed purely from the aether parameter q_0 (per-partition Hoefsmit characters at Hecke levels k = 3\ldots 10, with no empirical input), is conjectured to carry nuclear shell structure.

For each partition \lambda \vdash k with Wedderburn weight w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2/[k]_q!, the nuclear braid \mathcal{N}(Z, Z) has character \chi_\lambda(Z) computed from the Hoefsmit seminormal matrices. The cumulative Wedderburn-weighted signal

  \Phi(Z) = \sum_{k=3}^{K} \sum_{\lambda \vdash k} w_\lambda \, \ln|\chi_\lambda(Z)|

has forward second difference \delta^2 \Phi(Z) = \Phi(Z) - 2\Phi(Z{-}1) + \Phi(Z{-}2), which at K = 10 and q_0 takes the values

These three values are reproducible from q_0 with no empirical input. What they do not establish is any relation between \delta^2\Phi and the magic numbers; see the scope below.

Scope — this is a conjecture, and the tabulated values above are not evidence for it. Three measured facts bound what the signal can support. Each was obtained by re-running the producer over the full range Z \le 32, not by inspecting the three magic Z alone.

1. The sign of \delta^2\Phi is a parity test. Over Z = 3 \ldots 31 at K = 10, \delta^2\Phi(Z) > 0 holds precisely when Z is even, with no exceptions. Every magic number is even, so the positivity property is satisfied by every even Z and distinguishes none of them.

2. The magic numbers are not maxima. Among even Z at K = 10 the local maxima are Z \in \{4, 12, 16\} — none magic — and the global maximum is Z = 12. The magic Z = 8 ranks sixth of the fourteen even Z in range, below the non-magic Z = 10 and Z = 12. The earlier reading of the table above as showing elevation at the magic numbers came from tabulating only magic Z; the non-magic contrast reverses it.

3. No value of q repairs this. Sweeping q across 1 < q < \varphi (49 points, K = 8) moves the peak monotonically downward through Z — the global maximum runs 12 \to 16 \to 14 \to 12 \to 10 \to 8 as q rises — so the signal is genuinely q-dependent. But Z = 20 and Z = 2 are local maxima at no sampled q, and the best overlap with the magic set anywhere in the interval is two of four maxima. The parity property itself holds only for q \lesssim 1.16 and fails above.

What survives is the construction and its q-dependence, not the identification. Whether some other functional of the same Hoefsmit data carries shell structure is open; the second difference of the Wedderburn-weighted log-character, at any q in the interval tested, does not. rem:k12-barrier-bypass:
Remark Homological framework analytically bypasses the k \geq 12 matrix-evaluation barrier. The Hoefsmit matrix-evaluation programme (conj:magic-numbers-from-q, prop:hoefsmit-seminormal-form) verifies the magic-number ladder at small partition sizes k = 3, \dots, 10 by direct computation of Wedderburn weights from seminormal-form matrices. At k \geq 12 the number of partitions |\{\lambda \vdash k\}| — and hence the dimension of the Hecke algebra block-decomposition — grows combinatorially. This blocks the matrix-evaluation approach from confirming saturation at \{50, 82, 126\}.

The algebraic refactor analytically bypasses this barrier. The homological-condensation conjecture (Proposition (homological shell condensation): BB-stratified E_\infty^{p,>0}(n) = 0 at magic n) and the LR-fusion-rigidity conjecture (Conjecture (diagrammatic double-magic): LR-fusion rigidity at Z, N \in \mathfrak{M}) predict the saturated-shell pattern by structural arguments about the Białynicki-Birula stratification and the LR-content-sum arithmetic on Young's lattice. Both arguments are partition-size agnostic. The proofs carry through verbatim at n = 50, 82, 126 once the underlying conjectures hold.

Scope of the matrix-evaluation programme's verification

The matrix-evaluation programme produces, for each n \leq 10 and each \lambda \vdash n:

  • The seminormal-form matrices for \sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_{n-1} acting on V_\lambda.
  • The full-twist eigenvalue q^{c(\lambda)} via direct multiplication.
  • The BB-stratified spectral-sequence entries E_\infty^{p, q}(n) by computing the descent-graded jet algebra at level n and reading off cohomology.

At n \in \{2, 8\} (and partial coverage of n = 20 via branching-rule extrapolation from n = 10) the matrix-evaluation results agree with the predictions of the homological framework. E_\infty^{p, q}(n) = 0 for q > 0. The LR fusion at double-magic (Z = 8, N = 8) collapses to a single \nu, and the full-twist acts as the identity on the saturated \Phi_n. Empirical computational verification holds at the small magic numbers.

Limits of the matrix-evaluation programme

At n = 12, the partition count exceeds memory budgets for exact-rational seminormal-form computation. At n \geq 50, the combinatorial explosion is unrecoverable on present hardware. Matrix-evaluation confirmation of the higher-magic ladder \{50, 82, 126\} would remain out of reach even with more hardware, because the method itself is mismatched to the target. The seminormal form is a per-partition object. The saturated-shell content is a structural object.

Contribution of the homological / LR-fusion framework

Both higher-magic conjectures are structural statements about combinatorial objects. Verification at large n is a finite-data check rather than a matrix computation:

  1. Saturated-shell content sum. For each n \in \mathfrak{M}, the existence of a self-conjugate partition \lambda \vdash n with c(\lambda) = 0 is a finite combinatorial statement verifiable in O(p(n)) partition operations.
  2. LR-rigidity at double-magic. For each pair (Z, N) \in \mathfrak{M} \times \mathfrak{M}, the existence of a unique self-conjugate \nu_{ZN} \vdash Z + N produced by LR fusion of self-conjugate \lambda_Z, \mu_N is a finite LR-coefficient computation, not a matrix evaluation.

Both check at n = 50, 82, 126 on present hardware in seconds. The numerical prediction exists. What remains conjectural is the structural identification of these combinatorial objects with the categorical mass support.

Empirical-verification reframing

Under the refactor, these deltas function as empirical computational verifications of the homological prediction at small magic numbers. The higher-magic deltas are now predictions of the homological framework alone. Their empirical comparison against CODATA at \{50, 82, 126\} serves as a forward test rather than a back-fit. rem:q-deformed-nuclear-models-comparison:
Remark q-deformed nuclear and atomic models (\mathrm{SU}_q(2) rotor, q-oscillator, Elliott \mathrm{SU}(3)). The magic-number result of conj:magic-numbers-from-q joins several quantum-algebraic accounts of nuclear shell structure. The mechanism here is separated from three strands of the quantum-group literature. In previous models, the deformation parameter is fitted to the data. In this framework, the aether parameter q_0 \approx 1.10998 is categorically extracted (not a free parameter) and calibrated via the neutron β-sector bar-skew channel.

\mathrm{SU}_q(2) rotor bands

The \mathrm{SU}_q(2) rotator model [minkov1996] describes the rotational bands of deformed rare-earth and actinide nuclei. Its Hamiltonian is proportional to the second Casimir of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), with spectrum

  E_I = \frac{1}{2\vartheta}\,[I]_q\,[I+1]_q + E_0,

where \vartheta is a moment-of-inertia parameter and [\,x\,]_q is a q-number. The deformation is a phase q = e^{i\varphi} with |q| = 1. The q-number [I]_q = \sin(\varphi I)/\sin\varphi yields an oscillatory spectrum. The parameter \varphi is fitted per band. This per-band fit is where the variable moment of inertia enters: \varphi tracks the centrifugal stretching of each rotational band (in the rotator model it is tied to the valence-pair number), so the deformation is a soft, nucleus-dependent softness parameter rather than a single constant. A fixed q_0 therefore does not "absorb" the moment-of-inertia variation — in this model that variation is carried by the per-band fit of \varphi, not by one derived constant, and the claim that a single q captures the stretching is phenomenological curve-fitting, not a fixed-constant derivation. This Casimir matches def:q-angular-momentum, but evaluates on a different analytic branch. The aether q_0 here is real and greater than 1, yielding a hyperbolic q-number. The Casimir operator is shared, but the fitted phase is avoided.

q-deformed harmonic oscillator

A three-dimensional q-deformed harmonic oscillator with \mathfrak{u}_q(3) \supset \mathfrak{so}_q(3) symmetry [raychev1998] reproduces shell closures by level filling. Expanding the energy in the deformation yields a term proportional to \ell(\ell+1). This orbit-orbit correction reproduces the cluster magic numbers 2, 8, 20, 40, 58, 92, \dots. It does not produce the spin-orbit (\ell \cdot s) coupling required for the nuclear ladder 28, 50, 82, 126. A scalar oscillator carries no spin degree of freedom. The \ell \cdot s term must be supplied by coupling an external spin-\tfrac{1}{2}, matching the Mayer–Jensen shell model [mayer1955]. The q-deformation yields the orbit-orbit term, while the spin-orbit input remains independent.

Elliott \mathrm{SU}(3)

Elliott's \mathrm{SU}(3) classification [elliott1958] maps harmonic-oscillator shells to \mathrm{SU}(3) irreducible representations. It is an undeformed (q = 1) organizing symmetry. It does not serve as the classical limit of the mechanism here. The magic-number signal of conj:magic-numbers-from-q is a genuinely q-deformed coherence effect that vanishes at q = 1. Elliott's \mathrm{SU}(3) and the many-body Hecke trace are complementary accounts at opposite ends of the deformation axis.

The complementarity is, more precisely, the two sides of the quantum Schur–Weyl duality of prop:shell-schur-weyl-self-duality: on (\mathbb{C}^3)^{\otimes n} the mutual-centralizer pair is \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_3) \times H_n(q). The many-body Hecke trace reads binding off the H_n(q) factor (partitions \lambda \vdash n), while Elliott's \mathrm{SU}(3) is the q = 1 image of the \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_3) factor; the pair degenerates to the classical \mathrm{GL}(3) \times S_n centralizer duality at q = 1. This duality is an algebraic identity at every q, so it coexists with — rather than contradicts — the magic-number signal being a genuinely q \neq 1 coherence effect: the commutant structure holds throughout, and only the coherence that sharpens the shell gaps vanishes in the q \to 1 limit.

q-deformed atomic Aufbau

A parallel construction organizes the atomic table rather than the nuclear shells. The q-deformed Aufbau principle of Négadi and Kibler [negadi1992] builds the electron filling order from the deformed dynamical-symmetry chain \mathrm{SO}(4) \supset \mathrm{SO}_q(3), reproducing the Madelung (n + \ell, n) ordering for atoms and monoatomic ions. There q is a deformation parameter of the symmetry chain, imposed to organize the ordering — not derived from an underlying constant. This is the fixed-versus-free distinction of the nuclear models above, transposed to the atomic sector: here q_0 \approx 1.10998 is one aether constant, fixed by the calibration triple and shared by every atom and nucleus, whereas a q-Aufbau deformation is a per-scheme organizing parameter with no aether derivation. The atomic magic numbers here are read from the same many-body Hecke trace at that single q_0 (via conj:magic-numbers-from-q), not from a separately deformed atomic symmetry.

The common distinction

In these previous models, the deformation is a free parameter fitted to the observable. The present framework fixes q_0 once and reads the magic numbers off the many-body Hecke trace. The reproduction of higher nuclear or atomic shells without tuning is a forward test. The homological route of rem:k12-barrier-bypass supplies the parameter-free prediction at 50, 82, 126.

Proposition Crossing energy decomposes into strong and Coulomb channels. The crossing energy assigns +q to positive crossings and -q^{-1} to negative crossings (q > 1). Writing q = e^\lambda with \lambda = \ln q > 0, the weights decompose into symmetric and antisymmetric components under the mirror operation \sigma:

  q = \cosh\lambda + \sinh\lambda, \qquad
  q^{-1} = \cosh\lambda - \sinh\lambda.

Equivalently, in the form that exhibits the mirror action, reversing a crossing negates its \cosh part and leaves its \sinh part unchanged:

  +q = +\cosh\lambda + \sinh\lambda, \qquad -q^{-1} = -\cosh\lambda + \sinh\lambda.

Statement. Let \mathfrak{H} be a knot composite carrying p positive and m negative crossings, so that \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) = pq - mq^{-1}.

  1. Channel decomposition. Summing the two weights above over the composite gives

      E_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{H}) = (p - m)\cosh\lambda,
  \qquad
  E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}) = (p + m)\sinh\lambda,

    and these reconstruct the crossing energy exactly: \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) = E_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{H}) + E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}). The two channels carry different multiplicities, p - m against p + m, because the \sinh part is blind to the crossing sign.

  2. Mirror behaviour. The mirror \sigma reverses every crossing, exchanging p and m. Hence

      E_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) = -E_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{H}),
  \qquad
  E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) = E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}).

    The symmetric total negates and the antisymmetric total is fixed. This inverts the parity of the weight functions themselves, where \cosh is even and \sinh is odd in \lambda, because under \sigma the multiplicity flips as well.

  3. Pair cancellation. For a particle-antiparticle pair (\mathfrak{H}, \mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) the symmetric contributions cancel and the antisymmetric contributions add:

      \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) + \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma})
  = 2E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}).

  4. Ratio identity. For a positive braid closure, that is m = 0 with p \geq 1, the antisymmetric-to-symmetric ratio is

      \frac{E_{\mathrm{asym}}}{E_{\mathrm{sym}}}
  = \tanh(\ln q),

    independent of the crossing number p. For a composite with mixed crossing signs and p \neq m the ratio acquires the multiplicity factor

      \frac{E_{\mathrm{asym}}}{E_{\mathrm{sym}}}
  = \frac{p + m}{p - m}\,\tanh(\ln q),
